correctness.rationale: Frozen proof and narrowed repair checked. Every point of the skeleton is supported on at most s non-antipodal signed coordinate vertices. On a fixed nonempty support I match signs and adjust magnitudes monotonically to mass one; the triangle-inequality bound |t_I−1| within I is then attained, and the off-support cost is q−t_I. Maximizing t_I chooses the largest s coordinates. The origin at distance one and the balanced boundary vector with top-s sum below one give the separate sharp obstructions. Sufficiency follows by bounding the distance by q+1−2min(1,sq/d), affine up to d/s with endpoint values 1 and d/s−1, then equal to q−1≤λ. Equality has the correct ≥ endpoint by compactness. Convex hull and affine covariance follow from containing all coordinate vertices and the (1+λ)b translation term. The frozen supporting code and notes describe expected, not recorded, finite results; not replayed. The enumerated support test shares the face-wise distance lemma and cannot certify it.

It identifies the rank where the sharp obstruction switches from the balanced outer boundary to the missing origin, and determines feasibility at equality, not just a dimensional bound.
